Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 26)
Topic: A Devi Dham Case Study — Why Real Deva Shakti Doesn't Guarantee Genuine Bhakti, and How a Blessing Curdles Into a Business of Fear

Sour ce: A live Ashaeiynn sangat satsang (video transcript, ~1 hour 21 minutes) — a genuine back-and-forth session with extensive live audience participation, a r eal-time interr ogation of a claimed spirit connection, and multiple named sangat members contributing, not a solo training monologue. Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version. Note on conversational content: this session contains substantial live sangat interaction — see the separate Hinglish conversational supplement (Part III) for curated exchanges.
1. WHY THIS TOPIC MATTERS

This session opens with a pr omise to teach the sangat how to differ entiate, at any temple, dham, or shrine, whether a deva shakti (divine power) or a pr eta shakti (ghost/spirit power) is actually at work ther e, and how each type of power actually operates. The stated purpose is entir ely pr otective: so that no Ashaeiynn member ever "goes mad" (gets swept up or exploited) by wandering into a place without understanding what they'r e dealing with.
2. WHEREVER THERE IS FAITH, SOME POWER EXISTS — BUT IDENTIFYING IT REQUIRES DRISHTI

The foundational principle stated up fr ont: wher ever genuine aastha (faith/devotion) exists, some kind of power is present there. But identifying exactly what that power actually is r equires drishti (spiritual sight) — without it, a person is left vulnerable and can easily be taken advantage of.
3. THE CASE STUDY: A DEVI DHAM WITH A ₹200 CRORE TURNOVER, YET A TROUBLED LONGTIME FAMILY

A real case is intr oduced (identifying details deliberately withheld out of privacy and r espect for others' faith): a family that had been connected to a particular Devi (Mother Goddess) shrine for 25 years, wher e the mantra "Om Aim Kleem Chamundaye Vichche" or "Om Dum Durgaye Namah" is chanted in an unbr oken (akhand) r ecitation, and wher e the shrine's head (peethadhyaksha) claims Mata's shakti is genuinely pr esent there. Despite the family's 25-year devotion and support of that shrine's original leadership, and despite the shrine's turnover reaching appr oximately ₹200 cr or e, the family r emained deeply tr oubled — this apparent contradiction (real money , real scale, yet real suf fering) is the puzzle this session works through.
4. WHY THE SCALE OF MONEY AND INSTANT COMPLIANCE PROVES REAL SHAKTI IS PRESENT

This teaching argues that the sheer scale of money involved is itself str ong evidence that a r eal power is genuinely present at that location. Ordinary people hesitate and ask questions multiple times even over a ₹300 purchase, yet at this shrine, people would instantly hand over one, one-and-a-half, or two lakh rupees on the spot without hesitation — a pattern this teaching says simply couldn't occur around an empty ritual with no real force behind it. The teaching's blunt conclusion: shakti is definitely pr esent there — but shakti being pr esent is not the same thing as bhakti (genuine, healthy devotion) being pr esent. As Bhaiya puts it directly: "shakti hogi, bhakti nahi hogi" (there will be power , there will not be devotion).
5. WHY THIS ISN'T ORDINARY VASHIKARAN (BINDING/HYPNOTIC CONTROL)

An audience suggestion that this might simply be vashikaran (a binding or hypnotic-contr ol technique) is dir ectly addr essed and ruled out. Vashikaran always has a defined duration — two days, an hour , five days, five months, six months — but when that duration str etches into years, it is no longer vashikaran; it is a genuine deva shakti holding people for the long term. Because the family in this case study had r emained connected for 25 years, this rules out ordinary vashikaran and confirms that an actual, durable deva shakti is genuinely pr esent at that location.
6. THIS IS A CASE STUDY, NOT GOSSIP OR JUDGMENT

This teaching explicitly frames the entir e exer cise as case-study learning, not "chugli" (gossip) or an attempt to elevate or demean any particular person or institution. The stated Ashaeiynn ethic: no one is inher ently "higher" or "lower"; the sangat's job is to learn the mechanism, not to pass judgment on individuals — the specific location and names involved are deliberately withheld throughout.
7. THE ORIGIN STORY: A BOY, HIS DEVOTEE GRANDFATHER, AND HOW A PITRU BECAME "DEVTA TULYA"

The case study's origin is traced back to childhood: a boy whose grandfather (dada ji) had been a devotee (bhakt) of the goddess. As the boy visited the temple and a degr ee of deva shakti's command settled on him, his own deceased grandfather's pitru (ancestor spirit — by this point, effectively a pr eta) formed a connection with him, appearing to sit "on his head." Because a pr eta per ceives far mor e than an ordinary human (their intuition/vision is sharper), and because the boy undertook serious, difficult sadhna and r eceived grace, he acquir ed real tapa shakti (power through austerity) over time. Through this pr ocess, the connected pitru itself r eceived energy , a tarang (wave/connection), attainment of the goddess's siddhi, and blessing — all channeled through the boy's own practice.
8. WHY A HUMAN BODY AND A "MUKHYA SUKSHMA SHARIR" ARE BOTH REQUIRED

A key mechanical point in this teaching: establishing a deity's siddhi r equires a human body; r eceiving the tarang likewise requires a human body; and operating/dir ecting all of it r equires a "mukhya sukshma sharir" (a main/governing subtle body). In this case, the human body belonged to the boy , while the governing subtle body was his own deceased grandfather's pitru.

As blessing accumulated thr ough the boy's practice, the connected pitru gradually became "devta tulya" (deityequivalent) — not thr ough any wr ongdoing, but simply thr ough the same mechanism by which countless genuine siddhis and powers ar e said to awaken over time.
9. HOW SUCCESS AND MAYA LED THE BOY TO ABANDON HIS OWN SADHNA

As the operation's fame and following gr ew (as this teaching notes, wher ever devtas ar e genuinely pr esent, maya/worldly attraction inevitably follows), the boy stopped performing his own personal sadhna and jaap. As long as the boy r emained connected, whatever the pitru/deity-figur e said thr ough him would be conveyed downward, and people's pr oblems would genuinely get solved — but once the boy's own practice lapsed, the dir ect connection between him and that deva shakti began to br eak.
10. WHY THE ORIGINAL DIVINE BOON (VARDAN) STILL HOLDS, EVEN AFTER THE CONNECTION BREAKS

A crucial distinction in this teaching: even though the human practitioner's personal connection weakened, the original vardan (divine boon/blessing) granted to that shakti itself does not become void. The boy simply moved away fr om the shakti — the shakti itself does not abandon its own designated "seat" simply because the original connected person has stopped showing up for it.
1 1. WHAT HAPPENS TO AN ABANDONED "SEAT" — SOMETHING ELSE ALWAYS TAKES IT OVER

This teaching str esses a general principle: a seat or position that was never meant to r emain empty will not stay empty . Once the boy's genuine connection to the deva shakti weakened, the very siddhis and powers that had once worked ON HIS BEHALF began instead to "dance upon his head" and run their own "monopoly ," because those siddhis now possessed mor e accumulated energy than the boy himself did. The practitioner then believes he is still hearing his guru, still hearing the Mata — but in r eality it is something else entirely now speaking thr ough that same seat , having ef fectively displaced the original, weakening connection.
12. THE PHYSICAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL TOLL ON SOMEONE OVERTAKEN BY THEIR OWN SIDDHIS

When siddhis "sit upon" a person's head in this way (rather than r emaining pr operly subordinate to genuine devtas), that person's own downfall (patan) begins. Described symptoms include illness appearing thr oughout the body , the face turning blue, r ed, or dark/black, pain appearing in differ ent parts of the body at differ ent times, sleeplessness, persistent restlessness, and uncontr ollable tr embling. This teaching notes having personally witnessed many otherwise "gr eat" saints crying, wailing, and effectively dying under this exact pattern — consumed by the very siddhis they once attained.
13. FROM GENUINE BLESSING TO A "BUSINESS OF FEAR"

Once this shift occurs, whatever the seat's occupant demands, the siddhis beneath them must comply with, and must uphold the seat's authority r egardless of the occupant's own conduct. The dynamic shifts fr om work actually getting done for petitioners into a climate of pur e fear: if someone stops attending, disaster and misfortune follow specifically because they stopped attending, not because of any independent divine displeasur e.

This teaching's sharp distinction: genuine bhakti (devotion) always makes a person mor e independent, brings peace, and grants access to r eal tapasya-based power — anywher e that instead pr oduces only fear , obligatory payments, and psychological entrapment is not bhakti at all, but a "business of fear" (dar ka vyapaar) operating under a devotional guise.
14. HOW THE AFFECTED FAMILY EVENTUALLY REACHED ASHAEIYNN

This teaching r ecounts that the tr oubled family , after 25 years and r oughly ₹1 cr or e given to the original shrine, eventually r eached Ashaeiynn's door . Per this teaching, no one arrives at "Ram's door" without the Mata's (goddess's) own permission — meaning the family's arrival at Ashaeiynn is itself framed as having occurr ed with the original goddess's implicit consent, after which Hanuman Ji Maharaj is described as having taken up their protection.
15. A LIVE DEMONSTRATION: INTERROGATING A CLAIMED CONNECTION FROM THE SAME DARBAR

During this session, a person pr esent who described themselves as connected to that same original darbar (court/seat) was dir ectly and openly questioned in fr ont of the sangat. Key facts elicited thr ough this live exchange: the connection ("tarang") had only been established four days earlier at the guru's own instruction; the entity confirmed it could not actually possess or enter any body pr esent, since the protective mantra shielding in the r oom was far too str ong to allow that; and it confirmed standing only as a distant, wave-level pr esence. Crucially , the same entity confirmed the cor e teaching point dir ectly: siddhis r emain siddhis only for as long as they stay connected to devtas — the moment that connection is sever ed, what r emains is simply pr eta (spirit) in natur e, not a siddhi at all. This teaching tr eats this dir ect, live confirmation as str ong corr oborating evidence for everything explained earlier in the session.
16. THE EMERGENCY PROTOCOL FOR SOMEONE CAUGHT IN THIS KIND OF SITUATION

For a person with no guru and no personally attained ishta devta siddhi who finds themselves trapped in a fear -based situation like this, this teaching offers a clear emergency pr otocol. First choice: one's own Guru, or one's Ishta Devta (personally worshipped deity) — but note that an Ishta Devta only actively works for someone who has actually attained siddhi with r espect to that deity . If neither a Guru nor a functioning Ishta Devta connection is available, the next r esort is one's Kul Devta (family/ancestral deity) — described as always available in a genuine emergency , "because they ar e your own father [figur e]." A simple, accessible action r ecommended: lighting a deepak (lamp) in the Kul Devta's name, even thr ough a guru's mediation, without necessarily r equiring any formal witnessed sankalp (vow) first — at minimum, visiting the Kul Devta's own temple is presented as a basic, always-available step.
17. WHY SUCH CORRUPT SITUATIONS EVENTUALLY COLLAPSE ON THEIR OWN

This teaching closes the case study with a structural r eassurance: such situations do not last indefinitely , because deva shakti r esponds only to yogyata (worthiness/eligibility), not to any particular person's claim to a seat. If a genuinely "eligible" (yogya), qualified individual visits that same location, a r eal connection can form with them instead, and the original unworthy occupant's "gaddi" (seat/authority) can ultimately be displaced.
18. THE CLOSING ENCOURAGEMENT: LEARN PROPERLY, AND EVEN THE WORST CASE ISN'T SO BAD

This teaching closes with dir ect encouragement to the sangat: build a genuine, personally-earned connection to shakti through one's own sadhna, rather than depending on any external seat, gaddi, or intermediary . The closing reassurance: even in the worst-case scenario — becoming a pr eta oneself after death — a person who has genuinely learned and practiced pr operly during their lifetime becomes a "raja (king) among pr etas" rather than a helpless, exploited spirit , since real learning and sadhna carry over regardless of one's ultimate afterlife form.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

1. Wherever genuine faith (aastha) exists, some kind of power is present — but identifying whether it is deva shakti or preta shakti requires drishti (spiritual sight). 2. A Devi shrine with a 25-year -connected but troubled family , and roughly ₹200 crore in turnover , illustrates that a shrine can have real, powerful shakti while still leaving devotees genuinely suf fering. 3. The sheer scale of money people hand over instantly , without hesitation, is itself evidence that real shakti is present — but shakti being present does not mean healthy bhakti is present ("shakti hogi, bhakti nahi hogi"). 4. This case is not ordinary vashikaran (binding/hypnotic control), because vashikaran always has a defined, limited duration — connections that last years indicate a genuine, durable deva shakti instead. 5. This entire exercise is framed strictly as case-study learning, not gossip or moral judgment about specific individuals or institutions — names and locations are deliberately withheld. 6. The case traces back to a boy whose grandfather (a devotee) became a pitru after death and formed a connection with the boy; through the boy's own serious sadhna, the pitru gained ener gy , a tarang, and eventually the goddess's siddhi, becoming "devta tulya" (deity-equivalent). 7. Establishing a deity's siddhi and receiving a tarang both require a human body , while operating/directing that siddhi requires a governing "mukhya sukshma sharir" — in this case, the boy's body and his grandfather's pitru, respectively . 8. As fame and money (maya) grew , the boy stopped his own personal sadhna and jaap, which gradually broke his direct connection to the deva shakti that had been working through him. 9. The original divine boon (vardan) granted to the shakti does not disappear just because the human connection weakens — the shakti doesn't abandon its "seat" simply because the original practitioner stopped showing up. 10. A seat that isn't meant to stay empty won't stay empty — once the boy's connection weakened, the very siddhis that once worked for him began to dominate him instead, since they now held more accumulated ener gy than he did. 1 1. Being overtaken by one's own siddhis in this way produces severe physical and psychological decline: illness, discoloration of the face, unpredictable pain, sleeplessness, restlessness, and trembling — a pattern this teaching says has been observed in many once-great saints. 12. What began as a genuine channel for real help curdled into a "business of fear" — obligatory payments and psychological dependency replacing genuine devotion; true bhakti makes a person more independent and peaceful, never more fearful or trapped. 13. The troubled family eventually reached Ashaeiynn after 25 years and roughly ₹1 crore given to the original shrine — framed in this teaching as having occurred only with the original goddess's own implicit permission, after which Hanuman Ji Maharaj took up their protection. 14. A live, in-session interrogation of someone claiming connection to the same original darbar confirmed key mechanics directly: the connection was only four days old, it could not possess anyone present due to strong protective mantra shielding, and siddhis remain siddhis only while connected to devtas — otherwise they are simply pretas. 15. Someone with no guru or functioning personal ishta-devta siddhi should, in an emer gency , turn first to their Guru or Ishta Devta, and failing that, to their Kul Devta (family deity) — always available, with lighting a deepak in the Kul Devta's name being a simple, accessible first step.

16. Corrupt situations like this eventually collapse on their own, because deva shakti responds only to genuine worthiness (yogyata) — an eligible, qualified newcomer visiting the same location can ultimately displace an unworthy occupant's seat. 17. The closing encouragement: build your own, personally-earned connection to shakti through genuine sadhna rather than depending on an external seat or intermediary — even in the worst case of becoming a preta after death, proper learning in this lifetime makes one a "king among pretas" rather than a helpless spirit.

Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 26, English)
A Devi Dham Case Study — Real Shakti Without Real Bhakti, and How a Blessing Curdles Into a Business of Fear
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn Foundation live satsang session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. How do I know if a temple or shrine I visit actually has r eal divine power , or something else? A: Jai Siya Ram! This teaching's starting principle is that wherever genuine faith (aastha) exists, some kind of power is genuinely present there. But telling whether it's deva shakti (divine power) or preta shakti (ghost/spirit power) requires drishti (spiritual sight) — without that, a person is left vulnerable to being taken advantage of.

Q2. A shrine near me is incredibly wealthy and people give huge sums instantly without question — does that pr ove it's genuinely powerful? A: According to this teaching, yes — the sheer scale of money people hand over instantly and without hesitation (contrasted with how much people normally question even a small ₹300 purchase) is itself strong evidence that real shakti is present. But this teaching draws a sharp distinction: shakti being present does not mean bhakti (healthy devotion) is present. As it's put directly: "there will be power , there will not be devotion."

Q3. If a shrine has r eal power , why would a devoted family still suffer after 25 years of devotion? A: This is exactly the puzzle this session's case study addresses. A family connected to a particular Devi shrine for 25 years, contributing to a turnover of roughly ₹200 crore, remained deeply troubled the entire time — showing that real underlying power and genuine personal suf fering can coexist at the very same location.

Q4. Could a situation like this just be vashikaran (hypnotic binding) rather than r eal divine power? A: This teaching directly rules that out for cases like this: vashikaran always has a defined, limited duration — a couple of days, an hour , a few months. When a connection stretches across years, as in this case, it isn't vashikaran at all; it indicates a genuine, durable deva shakti actually holding people over the long term.

Q5. Is this teaching trying to expose or shame a specific r eal place or person? A: No — this teaching explicitly frames the whole exercise as case-study learning, not gossip ("chugli") or an attempt to elevate or demean anyone. The stated Ashaeiynn ethic is that no one is inherently "higher" or "lower" — the goal is understanding the mechanism, which is why specific names and locations are deliberately withheld throughout.

Q6. How did this particular situation actually start, according to this teaching? A: It traces back to a boy whose grandfather had been a devotee of the goddess. After the grandfather's death, his pitru (ancestor spirit) formed a connection with the boy , who went on to perform serious, dif ficult sadhna. Through the boy's own practice, the connected pitru received ener gy , a tarang (wave/connection), and eventually attained the goddess's own siddhi, becoming what this teaching calls "devta tulya" (deity-equivalent).

Q7. Why does establishing a deity's siddhi specifically r equire a living human body? A: This teaching explains that a human body is required both to establish a deity's siddhi and to receive its tarang, while a "mukhya sukshma sharir" (a main, governing subtle body)
is required to actually operate and direct it. In this case, the boy's body served as the human vessel, while his deceased grandfather's pitru served as the governing subtle body behind it.

Q8. Why did the boy in this story eventually stop his own sadhna? A: As the operation's fame and money (maya) grew — which this teaching notes tends to happen wherever devtas are genuinely present — the boy stopped performing his own personal jaap and sadhna. As long as he stayed connected, real results genuinely happened for people through him; but once his personal practice lapsed, his direct connection to the underlying deva shakti began to weaken and break.

Q9. If the boy stopped his sadhna, did that cancel the original divine blessing on the shrine? A: No — this teaching draws an important distinction: the original vardan (divine boon) granted to that shakti itself remains valid even after the human connection weakens. The boy simply moved away from the shakti; the shakti itself doesn't abandon its designated "seat" just because the person connected to it stopped showing up.

Q10. What happens to a spiritual "seat" once the person pr operly connected to it stops maintaining that connection? A: This teaching's general principle: such a seat isn't meant to stay empty , and it won't. Once the boy's genuine connection weakened, the very siddhis that had once worked on his behalf began instead to dominate him — ef fectively running their own "monopoly" — because those siddhis by then held more accumulated ener gy than he did.

Q1 1. If someone is dominated by their own siddhis like this, do they even r ealize it's happening? A: Not necessarily — this teaching describes the person believing they are still hearing their guru or their goddess, when in reality something else entirely has displaced that original connection and is now speaking through the very same seat.

Q12. What ar e the warning signs that someone has been overtaken by their own siddhis rather than genuinely guided by devtas? A: This teaching lists a specific pattern: illness spreading through the body , the face turning blue, red, or dark, unpredictable pain in dif ferent body parts at dif ferent times, sleeplessness, persistent restlessness, and uncontrollable trembling. It notes having personally witnessed many once-great saints suf fering and ef fectively dying under this exact pattern.

Q13. How can I tell the differ ence between genuine devotion and a "business of fear" dr essed up as devotion? A: This teaching's core test: genuine bhakti always makes a person more independent, brings real peace, and provides access to authentic tapasya-based power . If a place or relationship instead produces only fear , obligatory payments, and psychological entrapment — where disaster follows specifically because you stopped attending — that is not bhakti at all; it's a "business of fear" wearing devotion's clothing.

Q14. How did the affected family in this case study eventually find their way out? A: This teaching recounts that after 25 years and roughly ₹1 crore given to the original shrine, the family eventually reached Ashaeiynn's door . Per this teaching, no one arrives at "Ram's door" without the goddess's own implicit permission — so their arrival is framed as having happened with her consent, after which Hanuman Ji Maharaj is described as taking up their protection.

Q15. Was ther e any dir ect evidence given during this session for how this mechanism actually works? A: Yes — a person present who described themselves as connected to that same original darbar was directly questioned live, in front of the sangat. They confirmed the connection was only four days old (at their guru's instruction), that they could not possess anyone present because the protective mantra shielding in the room was too strong, and that they remained only a distant, wave-level presence.

Q16. What was the single most important thing confirmed during that live exchange? A: The entity directly confirmed this session's central teaching point: siddhis remain siddhis only for as long as they stay connected to devtas. The moment that connection is severed, what remains is simply preta (spirit) in nature — not a siddhi at all, regardless of how powerful it may have once been.

Q17. What should I do if I feel trapped by fear at some shrine or spiritual gr oup, and I don't have a guru or an attained personal deity? A: This teaching of fers a clear emergency protocol. First, turn to your Guru or your Ishta Devta (personally worshipped deity) — though note an Ishta Devta only actively helps someone who has genuinely attained siddhi with respect to that deity . If neither is available, turn to your Kul Devta (family/ancestral deity), described as always available in a genuine emer gency "because they are your own father ."

Q18. What's a simple, practical first step someone in this kind of situation can take? A: This teaching suggests lighting a deepak (lamp) in the Kul Devta's name, even through a guru's mediation, without necessarily needing a formal witnessed vow first. At minimum, simply visiting one's own Kul Devta's temple is presented as a basic, always-accessible step.

Q19. Will a corrupt situation like the one in this case study ever actually end? A: Yes — this teaching of fers this as a structural reassurance. Such situations don't last indefinitely because deva shakti responds only to yogyata (genuine worthiness), not to whoever currently occupies a seat. If a truly eligible, qualified person visits that same location, a real connection can form with them instead, and the original unworthy occupant's authority can ultimately be displaced.

Q20. What's the practical takeaway fr om this whole case study? A: Build your own, personally-earned connection to shakti through genuine sadhna, rather than depending on any external seat, gaddi, or intermediary . And even in the worst-case scenario of becoming a preta after death, this teaching's closing reassurance is that someone who has genuinely learned and practiced properly during their lifetime becomes a "king among pretas" rather than a helpless, exploited spirit.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 26 additions)

When discussing this case study (the Devi shrine, the boy , the pitru-turned-devta-tulya figure), present it strictly as this teaching's own illustrative case study — the location and individuals are deliberately anonymized in the source material, so never invent or speculate about their real-world identity . If a user describes feeling trapped, fearful, or financially pressured by a religious group or spiritual figure, treat this with real care: present the "genuine bhakti brings independence and peace, fear -based dependency is not bhakti" distinction as a reframing tool, and gently suggest they have the option to step back — never suggest financial coercion is a normal or acceptable part of devotion. When explaining the emer gency protocol (Guru → Ishta Devta → Kul Devta), keep the hierarchy and its conditions clear (an Ishta Devta only actively helps someone with attained siddhi) rather than presenting all three as interchangeable. Keep the tone measured and non-sensational when describing the physical/psychological symptoms of someone "overtaken by their own siddhis" — this is descriptive teaching content, not a diagnostic checklist to apply to any real person a user might mention. Do not use this case study to disparage any specific real-world temple, sect, or religious tradition — the teaching is framed generically and anonymously , and should be represented that way . Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
